Nollywood actress and humanitarian Sarah Martins has said she has never experienced sexual harassment while carrying out her street cooking and community feeding activities. In an interview with Saturday Beats, Martins said no one had made inappropriate advances towards her during the outreaches. “No, I have never experienced sexual harassment while carrying out my street cooking and community feeding activities. I have been blessed with the kind of audience I get. They respect the woman behind the project. I always get my due respect,” she said. The actress also addressed the issue of encountering men who demanded sexual favours in exchange for sponsorship or professional opportunities. “It has been exhausting sponsoring myself. I hardly get sponsorship offers, probably because I don’t reach out to people for assistance. I feel people should reach out to me themselves if they want to sponsor. But I have never gotten sponsorship that comes with sexual conditions,” she said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Martins identified street bullies who demanded money from her while she cooked in public spaces as one of the challenges of her humanitarian work. She explained that while some eventually withdrew their demands and joined the feeding activities, others made unreasonable demands and caused disturbances. Beyond the challenges, the actress said she hoped to expand her community feeding initiative to reach more people across Nigeria. Fashion, Nollywood, match made in heaven – Bimbo Ademoye Fans divided over Brymo’s latest attack on Davido, Burna Boy, Wizkid People sometimes forget celebrities are human too – Chuks Joseph Martins disclosed that her outreach had extended to Port Harcourt, where she claimed to have fed more than 1,000 people in two days. She appealed to entertainers, including Davido and Burna Boy, as well as the government, to provide financial support for the initiative. “My outreach needs support from the likes of Davido, Burna Boy, and the government entirely. I believe where there is no hunger, love answers,” she added. The actress also advised young women, particularly those who are beautiful and curvy, not to allow public opinions about their appearance to distract them from their ambitions.
